compared: per scenario: the openings started, whether the opening was cancelled when the uses withdrew, every use's outcome in join order, and the openings after one more use
declared: The core's uses that can withdraw are futures dropped (`MemoryStack::opened`); a use that cannot is `MemoryStack::opened_as(true)`, what `open_in_background` calls (Node's join without a signal). The opening ends 'pg down' in both: Node's ensurePg and the core's held runtime install fail after their gate. A withdrawn use has no outcome in the core, so its outcome is the label `withdrawn`. The core's runtime errors read `postgres runtime: <text>`: the replay compares the text after that prefix. The runtime install's wait is the gate in both; an opening the last use withdrew from ends in the same failure once its gate opens
